title: Mujahideen
capsule: The Mujahideen as a collective political-military phenomenon in this dataset refers primarily to the Afghan resistance factions that fought the Soviet occupation of Afghanistan (1979–1989) and subsequently contested power through the civil war of 1992–1996, though the term has been applied to various Islamist armed movements across the Muslim world since the 1980s. The Afghan factions, organized into seven Peshawar-based parties recognized by Pakistan and funded substantially by the United States (via Operation Cyclone) and Saudi Arabia, expelled Soviet forces by February 1989 and toppled the Najibullah government in April 1992. Factional warfare among the mujahideen parties then devastated Kabul, killing tens of thousands of civilians and opening the political vacuum the Taliban filled in 1996. The designation in this atlas likely captures the residual armed groupings operating after the Taliban's own rise and through subsequent cycles of Afghan conflict.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Mujahideen designation covers a highly fragmented and spatially discontinuous set of armed factions rather than a coherent state; any territorial polygon is necessarily a coarse aggregation of contested zones of influence with low precision.
